text:
Start from config.py: it is the project's control panel for camera, detector sensitivity, YOLO, risk grading, stability, and audio behavior.
main.py only calls run_visual_guide_session(). The runtime constructs the camera, three detection sources, the stabilizer, and the approach-risk tracker.
For each frame the same pipeline runs: capture, perceive, assess, then caution. This separation makes each module testable and lets us tune behavior without rewriting the loop.

text:
The camera is monocular: it supplies ordinary color frames, not depth data.
Low resolution and buffer control reduce lag. Dropping old frames is important because a safety warning based on an old image can be worse than no warning.
Before the continuous loop, the system asks for an empty view and builds a median background from 12 frames. Median capture is robust to a brief moving object or exposure fluctuation.

text: box grows · distance falls · moves center/down · moves fast
textPreview: box grows · distance falls · moves center/down · moves fast

text:
There are two fast danger signals. Background difference finds anything that changed from the empty scene; frame-to-frame difference finds active motion.
Contours become bounding boxes. Very small regions are rejected as noise, and boxes covering too much of the image are rejected because camera movement can create one huge false region.
The primary candidate is selected mainly by closeness, then center direction, vertical position, source priority, and size.
YOLO answers 'what is it?' and is intentionally not the safety authority by default. Approach risk uses up to eight observations and requires size growth or falling estimated distance before lateral motion can become serious.

text:
A raw detection is not announced immediately. The box is smoothed, brief dropouts are held, and warning text must remain stable before it replaces the current output.
The message rules are simple to explain: far objects are ignored unless the approach tracker says medium or high risk; medium center objects receive caution; close center objects receive stop.
Audio is non-blocking. In the current beep configuration, audio is reserved for an approaching object ahead or for a warning containing a recognized car or bicycle. Repetition limits prevent continuous alarm fatigue.
Close by emphasizing that the system combines responsiveness with filtering: it reacts quickly to an urgent center danger but suppresses flicker, lateral-only motion, and repeated messages.
